title: Rings and ring strain
goals: Say where ring strain comes from

sections.title: Cyclopropane: angle strain and bent bonds
sections.html:
A tetrahedral carbon wants bond angles of 109.5°. In cyclopropane the ring forces 60°. That squeeze is angle strain.

[[mol:C1CC1]]

The orbitals cannot point along the edges of the triangle, so they overlap off to the side and make bent bonds: less overlap, a weaker bond. C-C in propane 88 kcal/mol, in cyclopropane 65.

micro.t: Why less overlap means a weaker bond
micro.h: A sigma bond is strongest when the two orbitals point straight at each other.

macro.h: Strained rings open easily. The epoxide in the past exam's Question 4B is opened by methoxide for exactly this reason.

why.q: Why is the C-C bond of cyclopropane weaker than that of propane?
why.a: Its orbitals overlap off-axis (bent bonds), so there is less overlap.

sections.title: Torsional strain: eclipsed bonds
sections.html:
Look down any C-C bond of cyclopropane and every C-H bond is eclipsed: six eclipsing interactions. That is torsional strain. Ring strain = angle strain + torsional strain.

[[newman:H,H,C|H,H,C|0]]

summary: Ring strain is angle strain plus torsional strain.
